pages.subtext: For shared reading with a grown-up.
pages.alt: A small open book beside a circular version stamp marked 1.0.0.

pages.text: Mia had a BIG question.
pages.subtext: Pip leaned closer to listen.
pages.alt: Mia looks up at a large question mark while Pip leans toward her.

pages.text: Can I find nothing?
pages.subtext: Mia wondered where to look first.
pages.alt: Mia and Pip look through a round magnifying frame at an open shelf.

pages.text:
Mia opened a box.
There was no toy inside.
pages.subtext: Is this nothing?
pages.alt: An open blue box has no toy inside. Mia points toward it and Pip stands beside it.

pages.text:
The box was present.
Mia was looking.
The question was happening.
pages.subtext: An empty box was not no presented thing.
pages.alt: The same open box is outlined clearly. Eye, speech bubble and question symbols show looking, asking and recording.

pages.text:
Mia waited for a sound.
No one clapped.
pages.subtext: Is quiet nothing?
pages.alt: Mia and Pip sit still. A pair of hands remains apart, showing that no clap occurs.

pages.text:
Mia was listening.
The quiet could be recorded.
pages.subtext: Listening and recording were happening.
pages.alt: An ear symbol and a simple record card show that Mia listens and makes a mark for the quiet interval.

pages.text:
Mia wrote the word:

NOTHING
pages.subtext: Did the word make nothing appear?
pages.alt: A sheet of paper displays the word NOTHING in large letters beside a pencil.

pages.text:
The word was written.
The paper was present.
Mia had made a record.
pages.subtext: The word was not nothing.
pages.alt: The written word, paper and pencil are each circled to show presented records.

pages.text:
Pip asked,
'What if no one shows anything?'
pages.subtext: Mia thought carefully.
pages.alt: Pip has a speech bubble while Mia pauses with a small thinking cloud.

pages.text:
Then there is no example
to point to, say, record or check.
pages.subtext: No hidden example has been supplied.
pages.alt: Four outlined spaces for pointing, speaking, recording and checking remain deliberately unfilled.

pages.text: Our checking question has two paths.
pages.subtext: An example is presented - or no example is presented.
pages.alt: A single path divides into two labelled routes: example presented and no example presented. Shape and text distinguish the routes as well as colour.

pages.text:
If an example is presented,
the presenting is happening.
pages.subtext: So the presented example is an occurrence - not nothing.
pages.alt: Path A ends at a clear card containing a star, speech mark and record line, showing a presented occurrence.

pages.text:
If no example is presented,
there is no counterexample to use.
pages.subtext: We do not pretend that a hidden example was supplied.
pages.alt: Path B ends at an open dashed frame labelled no presented example, with no object placed inside it.

pages.text:
Those are all the ways
our checking question can go.
pages.subtext: Presented, or not presented.
pages.alt: Both routes return to one complete bracket, showing that the declared checking paths have all been considered.

pages.text: Every example we can show, say, record or check is something.
pages.subtext: There is no presented counterexample.
pages.alt: Four symbols for showing, saying, recording and checking surround one bright occurrence mark.

pages.text: There is no nothing.
pages.subtext: This is the starting point for Smithian Fold Theory.
pages.alt: A strong root line grows upward into a branching pattern beneath the words There is no nothing.

pages.text: Our rule talks about what can be shown, said, recorded or checked.
pages.subtext: It does not pretend to describe what no one can present at all.
pages.alt: A solid circle encloses four checkable symbols. Beyond it is an unlabelled open area with no claim written in it.

pages.text:
Put an empty bowl on a table.
What is present?
What is not inside it?
pages.subtext: Say exactly what you can point to or observe.
pages.alt: An empty yellow bowl sits on a table beside three prompt cards: present, not inside, and observed.

pages.text:
Listen for one short moment.
Did a clap happen?
Did listening happen?
pages.subtext: A grown-up keeps the moment short and calm.
pages.alt: Mia, Pip and an adult sit comfortably with a small timer and unclapped hands.

pages.text:
Draw or tell what you noticed.
Ask someone else to check.
pages.subtext: A second check may agree or disagree.
pages.alt: Two people compare a simple drawing and a spoken record. Equal and not-equal symbols show that checks may agree or disagree.

pages.text:
Keep what happened.
Do not hide a disagreement.
pages.subtext: Honest checks help us learn.
pages.alt: A folder keeps two different observation cards side by side instead of discarding either one.

pages.text:
Something was here:
Your question.
Your check.
Your record.

pages.alt: Mia and Pip place a question card, check card and record card together beside the closed blue box.
